_meta.title: GridWise synthetic test scenarios
_meta.purpose: Paraphrase robustness and boundary coverage beyond the public pack.
_meta.note: expected_directives lists the intended ground truth per note, in note_index order.

scenarios.label: Solar reduction: percent-remaining wording
scenarios.rationale: 24h clock wording; factor is the remaining fraction.

operator_notes: PV production will drop to about 20% between 13:00 and 15:00.

scenarios.label: Solar reduction: fraction wording
scenarios.rationale: Word-number window plus a fraction phrase.

operator_notes: Panel washing from one until three will leave roughly one-fifth of normal solar output.
Heavy cloud will halve rooftop output from 9 AM to 12 PM.

scenarios.label: Solar reduction: full outage
scenarios.rationale: A total outage is factor 0.0, still a solar_reduction.

operator_notes: The inverter is offline from 10 AM until noon, so expect no usable solar.
The charging circuit is locked out for maintenance between 1 AM and 4 AM.

scenarios.label: No discharge: relay testing
scenarios.rationale: Discharge blocked across the evening peak.

operator_notes: Relay testing means the battery cannot supply load from 5 PM until 8 PM.

scenarios.label: Charge and discharge outages together
scenarios.rationale: Two separate battery windows in one scenario.

operator_notes: No battery charging from 11 AM to 1 PM.
Battery discharge is prohibited from 8 PM to 10 PM.
Hold at least 150 kWh in the battery from 7 PM until 11 PM for critical loads.

scenarios.label: Reserve as a percentage of capacity
scenarios.rationale: 40% of 400 kWh capacity is 160 kWh; needs battery context.

operator_notes: Maintain a state of charge of no less than 40% of capacity from 6 PM to 9 PM.
Grid import must not exceed 140 kWh per hour from 6 PM until 10 PM.
Keep intake at or below 200 kWh between 7 PM and 9 PM while the substation is constrained.
Do not charge the battery from midnight until 3 AM.

scenarios.label: Boundary: window running to end of day
scenarios.rationale: Hour 23 boundary; the window must not wrap past midnight.

operator_notes: Battery discharge is unavailable from 10 PM until midnight.

scenarios.label: Distractor only
scenarios.rationale: Both notes are irrelevant; neither may invent a directive.

operator_notes: The registrar will publish the exam routine on Sunday.
Cafeteria hours change during the holiday.

scenarios.label: Three notes, mixed
scenarios.rationale: Two real directives plus a plausible distractor.

operator_notes: Expect a 60% reduction in solar between 11 AM and 1 PM due to haze.
Keep at least 100 kWh in the battery from 7 PM to 10 PM.
The IT department is migrating the mail server tonight.

scenarios.label: Bare clock window, four hours long
scenarios.rationale: Bare clock means afternoon, and one-until-four spans three hours, not two. Caught live: the model copied a two-hour example.

operator_notes: The battery charger is isolated for testing from one until four.

scenarios.label: Same start hour, longer window
scenarios.rationale: Window length must follow the end hour, not a memorised example.

operator_notes: Solar will be halved from 1 PM to 6 PM during the inspection.

scenarios.label: Single-hour window
scenarios.rationale: End-exclusive means a one-hour window is a single hour.

operator_notes: Do not charge the battery from 3 PM to 4 PM.
